outputs.t: Open circuits: scrap.
Boards exhibiting a broken trace shall be rejected.
Any bridging between adjacent conductors is cause for scrap.
Shorted nets are to be held for MRB disposition.
Mouse bites up to 0.15 mm are acceptable.
Edge nicks deeper than 5 mil shall be sent to the engineer for review.
Notches of 3 mil or more are rejectable.
Conductor width reduction from nicks or bites not to exceed 30%.
Where a nick takes out 25 percent or more of the trace width, the board goes to MRB.
Spurs longer than 100 µm must be removed.
Copper protrusions of 4 mil and above shall be reworked.
Spur reducing the spacing by over 20% is a reject.
Whiskers that cut conductor clearance 15% or more: hold for review.
Stray copper larger than 0.2 mm is not allowed and must be cleaned off.
Copper islands 8 mil or bigger are cause for rejection.
Residual copper splash shall be removed.
More than 3 copper specks per board: scrap.
Pinholes exceeding 75 microns shall be referred to engineering.
Pin hole 2 mil max.
Five or more pinholes on a board is rejectable.
Voids in copper are acceptable up to two per board.
Any missing hole is cause for rejection.
Undrilled holes found shall be put on hold for MRB.
Three or more missing holes per panel will result in scrap.
Missing drill hits exceeding one per board are to be reviewed.
Eroded pads are not acceptable.
Damaged land with loss of 0.25 mm or more is a reject.
Pad damage over 10 mil should be sent back for rework.
Missing pads: more than two per board means scrap.
A single missing pad shall be escalated to the quality engineer.
Defects of any type larger than 0.3 mm shall cause rejection.
No more than 4 defects of any kind per board are allowed.
Six or more flaws of any description: hold for MRB.
Any visible defect must be reworked before shipment.
Two or more open circuits on one board: put on hold and call the engineer.
Boards shall conform to IPC-A-600 Class 2.
Acceptance criteria: Class III per IPC-6012.
Class 1 general electronic product.
Inspection level - IPC Class 2 minimum.
Quality requirement: high reliability, Class 3.
